items.stem: A physician advising a municipal health program is asked which measure would describe newly identified cases of a condition during a defined period. Which measure is most appropriate?
items.correct_answer_rationale: Incidence concerns new events occurring over time.

distractor_rationales.B: Prevalence counts existing cases in a population.
distractor_rationales.C: Reliability describes reproducibility of a measurement.
distractor_rationales.D: Validity describes how closely a measurement corresponds to the state it is intended to measure.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design is identified when critically appraising research, not when selecting a frequency measure.

items.stem: A community clinic is planning services for people already living with a long-term condition. Which population-health measure best describes the number of existing cases?
items.correct_answer_rationale: Prevalence counts existing cases in a population and is useful for estimating chronic-care burden.

distractor_rationales.A: Incidence concerns new events over time rather than existing cases.
distractor_rationales.B: Reliability is reproducibility of a measurement, not a count of cases.
distractor_rationales.C: Validity concerns correspondence between a measurement and its intended state.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design does not describe the number of existing cases.

items.stem: During a public-health briefing, a learner proposes using incidence and prevalence interchangeably. Which response is most accurate?

options.text: Incidence concerns new events over time; prevalence counts existing cases.
Prevalence concerns new events over time; incidence counts existing cases.
The measures are distinguished by study design.

items.correct_answer_rationale: Incidence and prevalence address different population-health questions: new events over time versus existing cases.

distractor_rationales.A: Existing cases are counted by prevalence, not both measures.
distractor_rationales.B: Reproducibility refers to reliability, not incidence or prevalence.
distractor_rationales.D: This reverses the supported definitions of incidence and prevalence.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design is a separate consideration in critical appraisal.

items.stem: A public-health questionnaire produces the same result when it is repeated under the same conditions. Which property has been demonstrated?
items.correct_answer_rationale: Reliability is the reproducibility of a measurement.

distractor_rationales.A: Incidence is a measure of new events over time.
distractor_rationales.C: Prevalence counts existing cases in a population.
distractor_rationales.D: Validity concerns correspondence to the state the measure is intended to represent.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design is not a property of a measurement.

items.stem: A regional program wants to know whether a survey result closely represents the health state the survey is intended to measure. Which property is the program assessing?
items.correct_answer_rationale: Validity is how closely a measurement corresponds to the state it is intended to measure.

distractor_rationales.B: Reliability concerns reproducibility rather than correspondence to the intended state.
distractor_rationales.C: Incidence concerns new events over time.
distractor_rationales.D: Prevalence counts existing cases in a population.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design is identified when appraising research.

items.stem: A health team confirms that its assessment tool is reproducible but has not assessed whether the tool corresponds to the health state it is intended to measure. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The tool is valid because it is reproducible.
The tool is reliable, but validity has not been established.
The tool identifies the study design.

items.correct_answer_rationale: Reproducibility supports reliability; reliability alone does not establish validity.

distractor_rationales.A: A reproducible measurement can still be invalid.
distractor_rationales.B: Incidence is a population-health measure of new events, not a conclusion about reproducibility.
distractor_rationales.C: Prevalence counts existing cases and is not established by reproducibility.
distractor_rationales.E: Study design is a research-appraisal concept, not a conclusion about a tool's reproducibility.

items.stem: A physician reviewing a population-health paper wants to appraise its methods. What should be identified before inferring the study's strengths or limitations?

options.text: The study design and comparison structure
Only the number of existing cases
Only the number of new events

items.correct_answer_rationale: Critical appraisal should identify the study design; strengths and limitations should not be inferred without identifying the design and comparison structure.

distractor_rationales.B: Existing cases describe prevalence, not the study design and comparison structure.
distractor_rationales.C: New events describe incidence, not the study design and comparison structure.
distractor_rationales.D: Reproducibility is reliability of a measurement and does not identify study design.
distractor_rationales.E: Validity is a measurement property and does not identify study design.

items.stem: At journal club, learners compare a randomized trial with observational studies. Which statement best supports a careful appraisal?

options.text: All study designs select, time, and compare participants in the same way.
Study design is irrelevant to critical appraisal.
The designs differ in how participants are selected, timed, and compared.
All study designs are measures of incidence.
All study designs are measures of prevalence.

items.correct_answer_rationale: Randomized trials, cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, and case-control studies differ in participant selection, timing, and comparison.

distractor_rationales.A: The designs are distinguished by differences in selection, timing, and comparison.
distractor_rationales.B: Critical appraisal should identify the study design.
distractor_rationales.D: Incidence is a measure of new events, not a property of all study designs.
distractor_rationales.E: Prevalence counts existing cases, not a property of all study designs.

items.stem: A public-health resident reads a paper but cannot yet determine whether it is randomized, cross-sectional, cohort, or case-control. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Identify the study design and comparison structure.
Use prevalence to determine the study design.
Use incidence to determine the study design.
Use reliability to determine the study design.

items.correct_answer_rationale: Critical appraisal should first identify the study design; strengths and limitations should not be inferred without its design and comparison structure.

distractor_rationales.A: The evidence boundary does not support inferring limitations before identifying the design and comparison structure.
distractor_rationales.C: Prevalence is a measure of existing cases, not a way to determine study design.
distractor_rationales.D: Incidence is a measure of new events, not a way to determine study design.
distractor_rationales.E: Reliability is reproducibility of a measurement, not a way to determine study design.

items.stem: A health authority receives reports from a cross-sectional study, a cohort study, and a case-control study. Before comparing their findings, which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Assume the studies have the same comparison structure.
Treat the names of the designs as interchangeable.
Identify how the studies select, time, and compare participants.
Assume all studies measure the same population-health question.

items.correct_answer_rationale: Critical appraisal requires identifying the study design because designs differ in how participants are selected, timed, and compared.

distractor_rationales.A: The supported claim is that designs differ in comparison structure.
distractor_rationales.B: The designs differ in how participants are selected, timed, and compared.
distractor_rationales.C: Reproducibility addresses reliability of a measurement, not the features distinguishing designs.
distractor_rationales.E: The appropriate first appraisal step is to identify each design and its comparison structure.
